title: September 2026 SNAP participation
question: What will USDA's first official print report for national SNAP monthly Persons participating in September 2026, without seasonal adjustment, expressed in millions?
resolutionSource: USDA national monthly SNAP participation table
resolutionRule: Resolve on the first official publication containing the September 2026 national monthly Persons total, without seasonal adjustment and including any disaster assistance incorporated in that total. Express the published figure in millions: multiply a value reported in thousands by 0.001, or divide a whole-person count by 1000000. Preserve the source's precision; whole-person counts correspond to six decimal places in millions. Retain the first published value and ignore subsequent corrections and revisions. The exact official publication date remains unverified.
drivers: Expanded work-related time limits applied through recertification
California's principal first discontinuance cohort falls after September
Three unobserved months and uncertain policy-driven momentum

The level-persistence base rate is June's 36.352716 million. Every observed change is negative, but recent losses have slowed: the last three average -0.392812 million per month, compared with -0.539879 million across all nine. The forecast uses the recent pace.

USDA's fetched implementation memorandum expands time-limit coverage from ages 18-54 to 18-64 and narrows the dependent-child exception from under 18 to under 14. The changes were effective July 4, 2025 and applied through applications and recertifications. Continued attrition is a plausible mechanism for the observed trend; applying an additional full nationwide policy shock would double-count effects already present in the history.

Earliest discontinuances were projected for September 1, 2026, but the principal first cohort of over 55,000 was projected for October 1, after July-September countable benefit months.

Prior/update/interval: Use a persistence prior updated by the average of the latest three monthly changes, with dispersion estimated from all nine successive changes in the fetched September 2025-June 2026 sample. sigma = 0.151798 million, calculated as the sample standard deviation of those changes. The one-month 80% half-width is 1.28*0.151798 = 0.194302 million. For three unprinted months and drift estimated from three observations, use 1.28*0.151798*sqrt(3+3^2/3) = 0.475940 million. This 2.449-fold widening reflects the forecast horizon and uncertain drift under changing policy implementation. No additional one-off or policy shift is imposed.
